findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:115 `protected lemma one [StarOrderedRing R] [DecidableEq n] : PosSemidef (1 : Matrix n n R)`; PosSemidef.lean:102 `Matrix.PosSemidef (fun _ _ : α => (1 : R))`.
findings.fix: Rename to `posSemidef_const_one`, or delete it and use `posSemidef_const_of_nonneg zero_le_one` at the two call sites (lines 170, 181).
findings.issue: `posSemidef_one` states `Matrix.PosSemidef (fun _ _ : α => (1 : R))` — the all-ones matrix — but Mathlib's `one` on this exact predicate means the identity matrix. In a file whose premise is that a kernel *is* a matrix, the name asserts the wrong matrix.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:325 `protected lemma pow ... : PosSemidef (M ^ k)`, whose `k = 0` base case is `.one` = the identity — exactly parallel to PosSemidef.lean:181 whose `n = 0` base case is the all-ones `posSemidef_one`.
findings.fix: Rename to `posSemidef_hadamard_pow` and `posSemidef_hadamard_prod` (matching Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard`), and update the doc list at lines 31 and the call sites in Basic.lean:298, SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:386, Function/Closure.lean.
findings.issue: `posSemidef_pow` states the *entrywise* power `fun a b => K a b ^ n`, but `Matrix.PosSemidef.pow` in Mathlib is the matrix power `M ^ k`. Same defect at line 166: `posSemidef_prod` names `fun a b => ∏ i ∈ s, K i a b`, which reads as a product of matrices while the content is the Schur/Hadamard product — the proof itself goes through `Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard` (lines 170, 183).

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:418 `theorem posSemidef_vecMulVec_star_self [StarOrderedRing R] (a : n → R) : (vecMulVec (star a) a).PosSemidef` — cited in the proof at PosSemidef.lean:97; `:356 posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self`.
findings.fix: Rename to `posSemidef_vecMulVec_star_self`, matching the Mathlib lemma this generalizes from `Finite` to arbitrary index types; update the doc list (line 28) and uses in FourierAtom.lean:82.
findings.issue: `posSemidef_star_mul` reads as the matrix `star A * A`, which Mathlib names `Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self`. The matrix actually stated is `Matrix.vecMulVec (star g) g` — the file's own private lemma proves this at line 77 — for which Mathlib's name is `posSemidef_vecMulVec_star_self`.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:297 `theorem posSemidef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec`; PosSemidef.lean:42 `open Matrix` with the declaration in `namespace TauCeti`.
findings.fix: Name the right-hand side, e.g. `posSemidef_iff_conjSymm_and_sum_nonneg`, and update uses in Basic.lean:186,198, SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:228, Gaussian/Basic.lean:152, Kernel/Finsupp.lean:265.
findings.issue: `posSemidef_iff` claims the bare `_iff` name for a characterization of Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef`, whose right-hand side (conjugate symmetry plus nonnegativity of every finite Hermitian form) is not named. Mathlib names its characterizations of this same predicate after their RHS.

summary: The new TauCeti/Analysis/Matrix/PosSemidef.lean states everything as Matrix.PosSemidef but names four declarations with matrix-operation words that Mathlib already owns for different matrices: posSemidef_one (all-ones vs identity), posSemidef_pow/posSemidef_prod (Hadamard vs matrix power/product), and posSemidef_star_mul (vecMulVec vs star A * A). posSemidef_iff also claims a bare _iff for a Mathlib predicate that already has a named _iff_ family.
